literature.headline_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期基孔肯雅病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 与病毒复制蛋白的串联成像揭示了寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒的复制复合体和RNA分子的细胞内动态。本研究鉴定了>200个高置信度的宿主病毒RNA相互作用因子,并通过共聚焦显微镜成像确认了SFPQ-ZIKV和SFPQ-CHIKV RNA的细胞内共定位。 [10.1038/s41467-026-77830-4]
分析结果显示,传播模式符合重力模型动态,住宅区域之间存在频繁的病毒传播交流。疫情的时间动态和强度与气候变量,特别是温度和降水量密切相关。 [10.1073/pnas.2621019123]
研究发现,感染和疾病的空间模式往往不同,高感染率出现在研究地点西边的一个大型墓地附近,但疾病率不一定高。感染在家庭中的聚类相关性非常弱(约0.2),但感染状态在小于200米的距离内存在相关性。 [10.64898/2026.09.15.26363072]

共记录了692,705例基孔肯雅热病例,其中2024年病例最多(33.52%)。东南地区占病例总数的48.22%,尽管存在地区变化:2021年和2022年主要在东北地区,2023年和2024年主要在东南地区,2025年则主要在中西部地区。女性占主导(60.48%),20至39岁和40至59岁年龄组合计占病例总数的64.32%,而肤色为“棕褐色”的人群占59.12%。治愈是主要结局,占92.58%的病例,而629例死亡(0.09%)被归因于该疾病。 [10.36557/2674-9432.2026v5n7p480-495]
应对高后果性人兽共患病:尼帕病毒的经验:如果说 COVID-19 展示了规模的重要性,那么尼帕病毒病则反复证明了速度的重要性。 [10.25259/ijmr_3319_2026]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Tandem imaging with viral replication proteins revealed intracellular dynamics of replication complexes and RNA molecules of Zika and chikungunya viruses. [10.1038/s41467-026-77830-4]

The analyses revealed a dispersal pattern consistent with a gravity-model dynamic, with frequent exchanges among residential areas. The epidemic's temporal dynamics and intensity were associated with climatic variables, specifically temperature and precipitation. [10.1073/pnas.2621019123]

The study found that infection and disease patterns often differed spatially, with high infection incidence near a large cemetery but not necessarily high disease incidence. Intracluster correlation of infection was weak in households (∼0.2), and infection status was correlated across distances <200 meters. [10.64898/2026.09.15.26363072]

A total of 692,705 chikungunya cases were recorded, with the highest number in 2024 (33.52%). The Southeast region accounted for 48.22% of the cases, although there was a regional shift: Northeast in 2021 and 2022, Southeast in 2023 and 2024, and Center-West in 2025. [10.36557/2674-9432.2026v5n7p480-495]

Responding to high-consequence zoonoses: The Nipah experience: If COVID-19 demonstrated the importance of scale, Nipah virus disease has repeatedly demonstrated the importance of speed. [10.25259/ijmr_3319_2026]

papers.title: Unraveling the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island.
papers.abstract: Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya virus epidemic in 2024-2025, with >54,000 confirmed cases. This is the second major chikungunya epidemic on the island, following the first one that peaked 20 years ago. It has been asserted that this new outbreak finds its origin in a single introduction event into the island, offering an opportunity to exploit viral genomic data to understand the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the introduced transmission chain. We sequenced >3,000 viral genomes collected during the epidemic. Harnessing this genomic dataset, we used several phylogeographic and phylodynamic approaches to unravel the paths taken by the transmission chain and the external factors that might have impacted its dispersal and epidemiological dynamics on the island. Our analyses highlight a dispersal pattern in line with a gravity-model dynamic with viral transition events being more frequent from and toward more populated areas. Our analyses reveal that the transmission chain was overall spatially intermixed, with frequent exchanges among residential areas. In addition, we show that the temporal dynamic and intensity of the epidemic were associated with climatic variables, namely temperature and precipitation. Our results also show that in theory, the population immunity-resulting from this epidemic and the previous one (2005-2006)-could be sufficient to explain on its own the decrease in the transmission rate that led to the end of the epidemic. While a short-term resurgence cannot be excluded, the risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus in the human population appears therefore relatively limited in the upcoming seasons.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island, following a previous major outbreak in 2005-2006.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved sequencing over 3,000 viral genomes collected during the epidemic to analyze the transmission chain and external factors impacting the dispersal and epidemiological dynamics on Réunion Island.
analysis.methods: Genomic data were analyzed using phylogeographic and phylodynamic approaches to understand the transmission patterns and the role of climatic variables in the epidemic dynamics.
analysis.main_results: The analyses revealed a dispersal pattern consistent with a gravity-model dynamic, with frequent exchanges among residential areas. The epidemic's temporal dynamics and intensity were associated with climatic variables, specifically temperature and precipitation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the role of population immunity from previous outbreaks in reducing the transmission rate, suggesting a relatively low risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus in the upcoming seasons.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and prevention strategies, particularly in understanding the impact of climate on chikungunya virus transmission and the potential for future outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on genomic data and the potential for confounding factors in the analysis limit the strength of the evidence. The findings suggest a relatively low risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus, but a short-term resurgence cannot be excluded.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island using genomic data, revealing a gravity-model dispersal pattern and the role of climatic variables in the epidemic's dynamics. analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the 2024-2025 chikungunya virus epidemic on Réunion Island, following a previous major outbreak in 2005-2006.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved sequencing over 3,000 viral genomes collected during the epidemic to analyze the transmission chain and external factors impacting the dispersal and epidemiological dynamics on Réunion Island.
analysis_en.methods: Genomic data were analyzed using phylogeographic and phylodynamic approaches to understand the transmission patterns and the role of climatic variables in the epidemic dynamics.
analysis_en.main_results: The analyses revealed a dispersal pattern consistent with a gravity-model dynamic, with frequent exchanges among residential areas. The epidemic's temporal dynamics and intensity were associated with climatic variables, specifically temperature and precipitation.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the role of population immunity from previous outbreaks in reducing the transmission rate, suggesting a relatively low risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus in the upcoming seasons.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance and prevention strategies, particularly in understanding the impact of climate on chikungunya virus transmission and the potential for future outbreaks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on genomic data and the potential for confounding factors in the analysis limit the strength of the evidence. The findings suggest a relatively low risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus, but a short-term resurgence cannot be excluded.

papers.title_zh: 解析2024-2025年Réunion Island 基孔肯雅病毒疫情的流行病学与传播动态。
papers.source_body_en: Réunion Island experienced a massive chikungunya virus epidemic in 2024-2025, with >54,000 confirmed cases. This is the second major chikungunya epidemic on the island, following the first one that peaked 20 years ago. It has been asserted that this new outbreak finds its origin in a single introduction event into the island, offering an opportunity to exploit viral genomic data to understand the epidemiological and dispersal dynamics of the introduced transmission chain. We sequenced >3,000 viral genomes collected during the epidemic. Harnessing this genomic dataset, we used several phylogeographic and phylodynamic approaches to unravel the paths taken by the transmission chain and the external factors that might have impacted its dispersal and epidemiological dynamics on the island. Our analyses highlight a dispersal pattern in line with a gravity-model dynamic with viral transition events being more frequent from and toward more populated areas. Our analyses reveal that the transmission chain was overall spatially intermixed, with frequent exchanges among residential areas. In addition, we show that the temporal dynamic and intensity of the epidemic were associated with climatic variables, namely temperature and precipitation. Our results also show that in theory, the population immunity-resulting from this epidemic and the previous one (2005-2006)-could be sufficient to explain on its own the decrease in the transmission rate that led to the end of the epidemic. While a short-term resurgence cannot be excluded, the risk of a large-scale circulation of the virus in the human population appears therefore relatively limited in the upcoming seasons.
papers.abstract_zh: Réunion Island在2024-2025年经历了一场大规模的基孔肯雅病毒疫情,确诊病例超过54,000例。这是继20年前首次疫情高峰之后,该岛的第二次主要基孔肯雅热疫情。有人断言,此次新的暴发疫情起源于一次单一的引入事件,这为利用病毒基因组数据来解析引入的传播传播链的流行病学与传播动态提供了机会。我们对疫情期间收集的超过3,000个病毒基因组样本进行了测序。借助这一基因组数据集,我们采用多种流行病学和系统发育动力学方法,解析了传播传播链的传播路径以及可能影响其传播和流行病学动态的外部因素。我们的分析显示,传播模式符合重力模型动态,病毒传播事件在人口密集地区更为频繁。此外,我们发现疫情的时间动态和强度与气候变量,即温度和降水量密切相关。研究结果还表明,理论上,由此次疫情和之前2005-2006年疫情所产生的群体免疫力,足以单独解释导致疫情结束的传播率下降。尽管不能排除短期内疫情的再次暴发,但病毒在人类群体中大规模传播的风险在接下来的季节中似乎相对有限。

papers.title: Spatial analyses of infection and disease during chikungunya and Zika epidemics in Managua, Nicaragua
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Zika (ZIKV) viruses have caused widespread epidemics across the Americas. After several years of minimal transmission, CHIKV is once again spreading in Nicaragua. We investigated spatial aspects of two chikungunya epidemics (2014, 2015) and one Zika epidemic (2016) in a prospective pediatric cohort in Nicaragua. We used generalized estimating equations, generalized additive and mixed-effects models, Kuldorff’s scan statistic, and intracluster correlations to analyze the infection and disease status of ∼3,000 initially uninfected participants during each epidemic. We found that the incidence of infection (# new infections/total population) and disease (# new cases/total population) often had different spatial patterns, demonstrating that high-infection areas may not exhibit much disease. High infection incidence was observed near a large cemetery west of the study site. The large 2015 chikungunya epidemic and 2016 Zika epidemic started near the cemetery, exhibited high infection incidence throughout the study site, and had extensive month-to-month changes in spatiotemporal dynamics. Clusters of excess infections were large and adjacent to the cemetery, while clusters of excess uninfected participants were found in the northern and eastern sections of the study area. Notably, the intracluster correlation of infection was very weak in households (∼0.2), and infection status was correlated across distances <200 meters. Similarities across the epidemics suggest that targeting interventions to the built, non-household environment may reduce epidemic potential in Managua. Overall, spatial analyses of epidemics that only use case data may substantially underestimate the full extent of viral transmission, missing identification of high-infection areas and opportunities for intervention.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨尼加拉瓜基孔肯雅和寨卡疫情的空间特征,以了解感染和疾病模式之间的差异以及建筑环境在疫情传播中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及尼加拉瓜的一项前瞻性儿科队列研究,分析了在三次疫情(两次基孔肯雅疫情,2014年和2015年;一次寨卡疫情,2016年)期间约3,000名最初未感染的参与者。
elements_zh.methods: 使用广义估计方程、广义加性混合效应模型、Kuldorff扫描统计量和聚类相关性来分析感染和疾病状况。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,感染和疾病的空间模式往往不同,高感染率出现在研究地点西边的一个大型墓地附近,但疾病率不一定高。感染在家庭中的聚类相关性非常弱(约0.2),但感染状态在小于200米的距离内存在相关性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,将干预措施针对建筑环境而非家庭环境可能有助于降低马那瓜地区的疫情潜力,突显了空间分析在理解病毒传播中的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究的结果可以为病毒传播的监测和干预策略提供信息,特别是在识别高感染区域和实施针对性公共卫生措施方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用前瞻性队列研究,以及疫情月度动态变化可能影响结果解释。

papers.title_zh: 尼加拉瓜马那瓜地区基孔肯雅热和寨卡病毒疫情中感染和疾病的空间分析
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Zika (ZIKV) viruses have caused widespread epidemics across the Americas. After several years of minimal transmission, CHIKV is once again spreading in Nicaragua. We investigated spatial aspects of two chikungunya epidemics (2014, 2015) and one Zika epidemic (2016) in a prospective pediatric cohort in Nicaragua. We used generalized estimating equations, generalized additive and mixed-effects models, Kuldorff’s scan statistic, and intracluster correlations to analyze the infection and disease status of ∼3,000 initially uninfected participants during each epidemic. We found that the incidence of infection (# new infections/total population) and disease (# new cases/total population) often had different spatial patterns, demonstrating that high-infection areas may not exhibit much disease. High infection incidence was observed near a large cemetery west of the study site. The large 2015 chikungunya epidemic and 2016 Zika epidemic started near the cemetery, exhibited high infection incidence throughout the study site, and had extensive month-to-month changes in spatiotemporal dynamics. Clusters of excess infections were large and adjacent to the cemetery, while clusters of excess uninfected participants were found in the northern and eastern sections of the study area. Notably, the intracluster correlation of infection was very weak in households (∼0.2), and infection status was correlated across distances <200 meters. Similarities across the epidemics suggest that targeting interventions to the built, non-household environment may reduce epidemic potential in Managua. Overall, spatial analyses of epidemics that only use case data may substantially underestimate the full extent of viral transmission, missing identification of high-infection areas and opportunities for intervention.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)和寨卡病毒(ZIKV)在美洲引发了广泛的疫情。在数年几乎无疫情之后,CHIKV再次在尼加拉瓜传播。我们对尼加拉瓜进行了一项前瞻性儿科队列研究,分析了2014年、2015年两次基孔肯雅疫情和2016年一次寨卡疫情中约3,000名最初未感染的参与者感染和疾病状况。我们使用广义估计方程、广义加性混合效应模型、Kuldorff扫描统计量和聚类相关性来分析每个疫情期间的感染和疾病情况。我们发现,感染率(新感染人数/总人口)和疾病率(新病例数/总人口)的空间模式往往不同,表明高感染区域可能并不表现出高疾病率。高感染率出现在研究地点西边的一个大型墓地附近。2015年的大型基孔肯雅疫情和2016年的寨卡疫情均始于该墓地,感染率在整个研究地点均较高,并且在疫情的月度动态中表现出广泛的变化。感染过剩的聚类区域较大,且靠近墓地,而未感染参与者过剩的聚类区域则出现在研究区域的北部和东部。值得注意的是,感染在家庭中的聚类相关性非常弱(约0.2),但感染状态在小于200米的距离内存在相关性。疫情之间的相似性表明,将干预措施针对建筑环境而非家庭环境可能有助于降低马那瓜地区的疫情潜力。总体而言,仅使用病例数据进行疫情的空间分析可能会显著低估病毒传播的范围,错过高感染区域的识别以及干预机会。
papers.summary_zh: 摘要 基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV)和寨卡病毒(ZIKV)在美洲引发了广泛的疫情。在数年几乎无疫情之后,CHIKV再次在尼加拉瓜传播。我们对尼加拉瓜进行了一项前瞻性儿科队列研究,分析了2014年、2015年两次基孔肯雅疫情和2016年一次寨卡疫情中约3,000名最初未感染的参与者感染和疾病状况。我们使用广义估计方程、广义加性混合效应模型、Kuldorff扫描统计量和聚类相关性来分析每个疫情期间的感染和疾病情况。我们发现,感染率(新感染人数/总人口)和疾病率(新病例数/总人口)的空间模式往往不同,表明高感染区域可能并不表现出高疾病率。高感染率出现在研究地点西边的一个大型墓地附近。2015年的大型基孔肯雅疫情和2016年的寨卡疫情均始于该墓地,感染率在整个研究地点均较高,并且在疫情的月度动态中表现出广泛的变化。感染过剩的聚类区域较大,且靠近墓地,而未感染参与者过剩的聚类区域则出现在研究区域的北部和东部。值得注意的是,感染在家庭中的聚类相关性非常弱(约0.2),但感染状态在小于200米的距离内存在相关性。疫情之间的相似性表明,将干预措施针对建筑环境而非家庭环境可能有助于降低马那瓜地区的疫情潜力。总体而言,仅使用病例数据进行疫情的空间分析可能会显著低估病毒传播的范围,错过高感染区域的识别以及干预机会。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨尼加拉瓜基孔肯雅和寨卡疫情的空间特征,以了解感染和疾病模式之间的差异以及建筑环境在疫情传播中的作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及尼加拉瓜的一项前瞻性儿科队列研究,分析了在三次疫情(两次基孔肯雅疫情,2014年和2015年;一次寨卡疫情,2016年)期间约3,000名最初未感染的参与者。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用广义估计方程、广义加性混合效应模型、Kuldorff扫描统计量和聚类相关性来分析感染和疾病状况。
analysis_zh.main_results: 研究发现,感染和疾病的空间模式往往不同,高感染率出现在研究地点西边的一个大型墓地附近,但疾病率不一定高。感染在家庭中的聚类相关性非常弱(约0.2),但感染状态在小于200米的距离内存在相关性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,将干预措施针对建筑环境而非家庭环境可能有助于降低马那瓜地区的疫情潜力,突显了空间分析在理解病毒传播中的重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 本研究的结果可以为病毒传播的监测和干预策略提供信息,特别是在识别高感染区域和实施针对性公共卫生措施方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用前瞻性队列研究,以及疫情月度动态变化可能影响结果解释。

papers.title: Perfil epidemiológico da febre de chikungunya no Brasil no período de 2021 a 2025 Epidemiological profile of chikungunya fever in Brazil from 2021 to 2025 Perfil epidemiológico de la fiebre chikungunya en Brasil de 2021 a 2025
papers.abstract: Introdução: A febre de chikungunya constitui importante problema de saúde pública no Brasil, apresentando variações temporais e espaciais relacionadas à dinâmica de transmissão do vírus. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar o perfil epidemiológico da febre de chikungunya no Brasil entre 2021 e 2025, considerando sua distribuição temporal, geográfica e características sociodemográficas. Metodologia: Trata-se de um estudo ecológico, descritivo e de abordagem quantitativa, realizado a partir de dados secundários do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN), obtidos por meio do DATASUS/TABNET. Foram incluídos os casos classificados como chikungunya cujo ano dos primeiros sintomas estivesse compreendido entre 2021 e 2025. Foram analisadas as variáveis ano dos primeiros sintomas, região de notificação, sexo, faixa etária, raça/cor, escolaridade e evolução dos casos. Resultados: Foram registrados 692.705 casos de chikungunya, com maior número em 2024 (33,52%). analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of chikungunya fever in Brazil from 2021 to 2025, considering its temporal, geographic, and sociodemographic distribution. Chikungunya fever constitutes an important public health problem in Brazil, with variations related to the virus transmission dynamics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was an ecological, descriptive, and quantitative study conducted using secondary data from the SINAN system, accessed through DATASUS/TABNET. The study included cases classified as chikungunya with the first symptoms occurring between 2021 and 2025.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed variables such as the year of first symptoms, region of notification, sex, age group, race/color, education level, and case evolution. It employed an ecological approach to examine the distribution patterns of chikungunya cases across different demographic and geographic factors.
analysis.main_results: A total of 692,705 chikungunya cases were recorded, with the highest number in 2024 (33.52%). The Southeast region accounted for 48.22% of the cases, although there was a regional shift: Northeast in 2021 and 2022, Southeast in 2023 and 2024, and Center-West in 2025. Female sex was predominant (60.48%), with age groups 20–39 and 40–59 years accounting for 64.32% of cases. The race/color group 'parda' represented 59.12% of the cases. The main outcome was recovery, recorded in 92.58% of cases, while 629 deaths (0.09%) were attributed to the disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant temporal and regional heterogeneity of chikungunya in Brazil, with a concentration of cases among women, individuals aged 20–59 years, and those of mixed race/color. This study provides a detailed overview of the epidemiological trends of chikungunya fever over a five-year period.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform targeted public health interventions, particularly in regions and demographics most affected by chikungunya, and emphasize the need for improved surveillance and vector control measures. They also highlight the importance of accurate data recording in notification systems.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on secondary data from SINAN, which may have limitations in completeness and accuracy. The evidence is strong due to the large sample size and the use of a well-established surveillance system, but the ecological design limits the ability to infer individual-level causal relationships.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides an epidemiological profile of chikungunya fever in Brazil from 2021 to 2025, highlighting its temporal and regional variations. It reports a total of 692,705 cases, with the highest incidence in 2024, and identifies the Southeast region as the most affected. The findings show a predominance of female cases, with age groups 20–39 and 40–59 years comprising 64.32% of all cases. The race/color group 'parda' was most represented, and recovery was the main outcome, observed in 92.58% of cases. The study underscores the need for enhanced surveillance and vector control strategies. While the ecological design limits causal inference, the large dataset and use of SINAN provide strong evidence for the observed trends.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析2021年至2025年间巴西基孔肯雅热的流行病学特征,考虑其时间、地理和社会人口学分布。基孔肯雅热是巴西重要的公共卫生问题,其变化与基孔肯雅病毒的传播动态相关。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为生态学、描述性和定量研究,使用来自巴西国家通知系统(SINAN)的次级数据,通过DATASUS/TABNET获取。研究纳入了2021年至2025年间首次出现症状的基孔肯雅热病例。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究分析了首次症状年份、通知地区、性别、年龄组、种族/肤色、教育水平和病例演变等变量。采用生态学方法,探讨基孔肯雅热病例在不同人口和社会地理因素中的分布模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 共记录了692,705例基孔肯雅热病例,其中2024年病例最多(33.52%)。东南地区占病例总数的48.22%,尽管存在地区变化:2021年和2022年主要在东北地区,2023年和2024年主要在东南地区,2025年则主要在中西部地区。女性占主导(60.48%),20至39岁和40至59岁年龄组合计占病例总数的64.32%,而肤色为“棕褐色”的人群占59.12%。治愈是主要结局,占92.58%的病例,而629例死亡(0.09%)被归因于该疾病。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了基孔肯雅热在巴西的时间和空间异质性,病例主要集中在女性、20至59岁人群以及肤色为棕褐色的人群中。本研究提供了基孔肯雅热在五年期间的流行病学趋势的详细概述。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果可以为针对基孔肯雅热高发地区和人群的公共卫生干预措施提供信息,并强调改进基孔肯雅病毒监测和控制措施的必要性。同时,也突显了在通知系统中准确记录数据的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究基于来自SINAN的次级数据,可能在完整性和准确性方面存在局限。由于样本量大且使用了成熟的基孔肯雅病毒监测系统,证据强度较强,但生态学设计限制了推断个体层面因果关系的能力。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of chikungunya fever in Brazil from 2021 to 2025, considering its temporal, geographic, and sociodemographic distribution. Chikungunya fever constitutes an important public health problem in Brazil, with variations related to the virus transmission dynamics.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This was an ecological, descriptive, and quantitative study conducted using secondary data from the SINAN system, accessed through DATASUS/TABNET. The study included cases classified as chikungunya with the first symptoms occurring between 2021 and 2025.
analysis_en.methods: The study analyzed variables such as the year of first symptoms, region of notification, sex, age group, race/color, education level, and case evolution. It employed an ecological approach to examine the distribution patterns of chikungunya cases across different demographic and geographic factors.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 692,705 chikungunya cases were recorded, with the highest number in 2024 (33.52%). The Southeast region accounted for 48.22% of the cases, although there was a regional shift: Northeast in 2021 and 2022, Southeast in 2023 and 2024, and Center-West in 2025. Female sex was predominant (60.48%), with age groups 20–39 and 40–59 years accounting for 64.32% of cases. The race/color group 'parda' represented 59.12% of the cases. The main outcome was recovery, recorded in 92.58% of cases, while 629 deaths (0.09%) were attributed to the disease.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the significant temporal and regional heterogeneity of chikungunya in Brazil, with a concentration of cases among women, individuals aged 20–59 years, and those of mixed race/color. This study provides a detailed overview of the epidemiological trends of chikungunya fever over a five-year period.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform targeted public health interventions, particularly in regions and demographics most affected by chikungunya, and emphasize the need for improved surveillance and vector control measures. They also highlight the importance of accurate data recording in notification systems.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on secondary data from SINAN, which may have limitations in completeness and accuracy. The evidence is strong due to the large sample size and the use of a well-established surveillance system, but the ecological design limits the ability to infer individual-level causal relationships.

papers.title_zh: 巴西2021至2025年基孔肯雅热的流行病学特征
papers.source_body_en: Introdução: A febre de chikungunya constitui importante problema de saúde pública no Brasil, apresentando variações temporais e espaciais relacionadas à dinâmica de transmissão do vírus. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar o perfil epidemiológico da febre de chikungunya no Brasil entre 2021 e 2025, considerando sua distribuição temporal, geográfica e características sociodemográficas. Metodologia: Trata-se de um estudo ecológico, descritivo e de abordagem quantitativa, realizado a partir de dados secundários do Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação (SINAN), obtidos por meio do DATASUS/TABNET. Foram incluídos os casos classificados como chikungunya cujo ano dos primeiros sintomas estivesse compreendido entre 2021 e 2025. Foram analisadas as variáveis ano dos primeiros sintomas, região de notificação, sexo, faixa etária, raça/cor, escolaridade e evolução dos casos. Resultados: Foram registrados 692.705 casos de chikungunya, com maior número em 2024 (33,52%). A Região Sudeste concentrou 48,22% dos registros, embora tenha ocorrido mudança do predomínio regional: Nordeste em 2021 e 2022, Sudeste em 2023 e 2024 e Centro-Oeste em 2025. Houve predominância do sexo feminino (60,48%), das faixas etárias de 20 a 39 e 40 a 59 anos, que juntas corresponderam a 64,32% dos casos, e da raça/cor parda (59,12%). A cura foi o principal desfecho, registrada em 92,58% dos casos, enquanto 629 óbitos (0,09%) foram atribuídos ao agravo. Conclusão: Os achados demonstram importante heterogeneidade temporal e regional da chikungunya no Brasil, com maior concentração de casos entre mulheres, indivíduos de 20 a 59 anos e pessoas de raça/cor parda. Ressalta-se a necessidade de fortalecimento da vigilância epidemiológica, das ações de prevenção e controle vetorial e da qualidade dos registros nos sistemas de notificação.

papers.full_text: Abstract Arthropod-borne, positive-sense RNA viruses encompass many human pathogens posing significant health threats worldwide. Understanding intracellular dynamics and host-factor interactions of the viral genome is essential for devising effective antiviral strategies. Here, we engineer dual-labeled Zika and chikungunya viruses incorporating a Mango-II aptamer for RNA pulldown and real-time imaging, achieving high-resolution imaging of flavivirus RNA in live cells. Tandem imaging with viral replication proteins revealed intracellular dynamics of replication complexes and RNA molecules of these viruses. We identify >200 high-confidence host interactors of viral RNA and corroborated 355 hits from existing data sets. Spliceosome factor SFPQ is as a common interactor decreasing RNA production in both viruses when depleted. Intracellular colocalization of SFPQ-ZIKV and SFPQ-CHIKV RNA is confirmed through confocal microscopy imaging of infected cells. Thus, we demonstrate Mango-II aptamer tagging as an innovative strategy for identifying spatiotemporal dynamics and virus-host interactions of viral genomes in positive-strand RNA viruses. Acknowledgements The authors thank the Huck Institute of Life Sciences at The Pennsylvania State University and the Microscopy facility for their technical support. We acknowledge the Indiana University School of Medicine Center for Proteome Analysis for sample preparation, mass spectrometry analysis, bioinformatics, and data evaluation in support of quantitative proteomics and phosphoproteomics experiments. Graphics were generated using GraphPad Prism, Cytoscape, and Inkscape. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the intracellular dynamics and host-factor interactions of Zika and chikungunya viral RNAs, essential for devising effective antiviral strategies. Arthropod-borne, positive-sense RNA viruses pose significant health threats worldwide, and understanding their dynamics is crucial.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved engineering dual-labeled Zika and chikungunya viruses incorporating a Mango-II aptamer for RNA pulldown and real-time imaging, achieving high-resolution imaging of flavivirus RNA in live cells. The research was conducted in live cells and utilized tandem imaging with viral replication proteins.
analysis.methods: The researchers used tandem imaging with viral replication proteins to reveal intracellular dynamics of replication complexes and RNA molecules of these viruses. They identified >200 high-confidence host interactors of viral RNA and corroborated 355 hits from existing data sets. SFPQ was identified as a common interactor decreasing RNA production in both viruses when depleted.
analysis.main_results: Tandem imaging with viral replication proteins revealed intracellular dynamics of replication complexes and RNA molecules of Zika and chikungunya viruses. The study identified >200 high-confidence host interactors of viral RNA and confirmed the intracellular colocalization of SFPQ-ZIKV and SFPQ-CHIKV RNA through confocal microscopy imaging.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as demonstrating the Mango-II aptamer tagging as an innovative strategy for identifying spatiotemporal dynamics and virus-host interactions of viral genomes in positive-strand RNA viruses. They identified SFPQ as a common interactor that decreases RNA production in both viruses when depleted.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment of Zika and chikungunya viruses by providing insights into their intracellular dynamics and host interactions. This can aid in the development of targeted antiviral strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of live cells and the need for further validation of the identified host interactors. The evidence strength is moderate due to the preliminary nature of the findings and the need for additional research to confirm the role of SFPQ in RNA production.

analysis.summary_en: This study engineered dual-labeled Zika and chikungunya viruses to visualize their RNA dynamics in live cells, identifying >200 host interactors and confirming SFPQ as a common interactor that decreases RNA production. The findings provide insights for developing antiviral strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒RNA的细胞内动态及其与宿主因子的相互作用,这对于制定有效的抗病毒药物策略至关重要。蚊媒、正链RNA病毒对全球健康构成重大威胁,了解其动态至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及工程化双标记的寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒,结合Mango-II适配体用于RNA沉淀和实时成像,实现了在活细胞中对黄病毒RNA的高分辨率成像。研究在活细胞中进行,并利用病毒复制蛋白的串联成像。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员使用病毒复制蛋白的串联成像揭示了这些病毒复制复合体和RNA分子的细胞内动态。他们鉴定了>200个高置信度的宿主病毒RNA相互作用因子,并验证了现有数据集中的355个结果。SFPQ被鉴定为一个共同的相互作用因子,当其被耗尽时,会减少这两种病毒的RNA产量。
elements_zh.main_results: 与病毒复制蛋白的串联成像揭示了寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒的复制复合体和RNA分子的细胞内动态。本研究鉴定了>200个高置信度的宿主病毒RNA相互作用因子,并通过共聚焦显微镜成像确认了SFPQ-ZIKV和SFPQ-CHIKV RNA的细胞内共定位。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证明Mango-II适配体标记是一种创新策略,用于识别正链RNA病毒中病毒基因组的时空动态及其与病毒宿主的相互作用。他们鉴定出SFPQ是一个共同的相互作用因子,当其被耗尽时,会减少这两种病毒的RNA产量。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒的监测、诊断和治疗提供信息,通过揭示其细胞内动态和宿主相互作用。这有助于制定针对性的抗病毒药物策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用活细胞以及需要进一步验证所鉴定的宿主相互作用因子。由于发现的初步性质以及需要进一步研究以确认SFPQ在RNA产量中的作用,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用病毒复制蛋白的串联成像揭示了这些病毒复制复合体和RNA分子的细胞内动态。他们鉴定了>200个高置信度的宿主病毒RNA相互作用因子,并验证了现有数据集中的355个结果。SFPQ被鉴定为一个共同的相互作用因子,当其被耗尽时,会减少这两种病毒的RNA产量。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与病毒复制蛋白的串联成像揭示了寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒的复制复合体和RNA分子的细胞内动态。本研究鉴定了>200个高置信度的宿主病毒RNA相互作用因子,并通过共聚焦显微镜成像确认了SFPQ-ZIKV和SFPQ-CHIKV RNA的细胞内共定位。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证明Mango-II适配体标记是一种创新策略,用于识别正链RNA病毒中病毒基因组的时空动态及其与病毒宿主的相互作用。他们鉴定出SFPQ是一个共同的相互作用因子,当其被耗尽时,会减少这两种病毒的RNA产量。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为寨卡病毒和基孔肯雅病毒的监测、诊断和治疗提供信息,通过揭示其细胞内动态和宿主相互作用。这有助于制定针对性的抗病毒药物策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用活细胞以及需要进一步验证所鉴定的宿主相互作用因子。由于发现的初步性质以及需要进一步研究以确认SFPQ在RNA产量中的作用,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Solanaceae-Derived Spirostane Saponins Inhibit Dengue Virus Replication and Viral Protein Expression and Exhibit Activity Against Multiple Arboviruses.
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.

papers.title_zh: 来自茄科植物的螺甾烷皂苷抑制登革病毒复制和病毒蛋白表达,并对多种虫媒病毒具有活性。
papers.source_body_en: Mosquito-borne arboviruses, including dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), represent a growing global health burden, yet no specific antiviral therapies are currently available for most of these infections. This unmet need highlights the importance of identifying novel antiviral compounds from biologically relevant sources such as plant-derived natural products. In this study, a bioactivity-guided approach was applied to methanolic extracts from eight Solanaceae species to identify compounds with antiviral activity against DENV-2 in Vero cells. Five extracts significantly reduced viral infectivity, with Solanum ovalifolium and Cestrum sp. achieving complete inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations. Subsequent fractionation and purification led to the isolation of four spirostane-type steroidal saponins, structurally characterized by UPLC-DAD-MS and 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy. Functional assays demonstrated that these compounds inhibit DENV replication, as evidenced by marked reductions in viral RNA levels, NS1 and NS3 protein expression, and infectious viral titers. Stage-specific analyses revealed that their antiviral activity is primarily associated with intracellular phases of the viral life cycle, consistent with inhibition of viral replication and/or protein processing. Molecular docking analyses supported these findings by predicting favorable interactions with key viral enzymes, particularly NS5 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and NS3 helicase/protease. Importantly, the isolated compounds retained antiviral activity against ZIKV and CHIKV, indicating cross-arboviral efficacy. Together, these findings identify spirostane saponins as promising antiviral scaffolds and support their further development as broad-spectrum antiviral agents.
papers.abstract_zh: 由蚊子传播的虫媒病毒,包括登革病毒(DENV)、寨卡病毒(ZIKV)和基孔肯雅病毒(CHIKV),构成了日益增长的全球健康负担,但目前针对这些感染的特定抗病毒药物疗法尚不普及。这种未满足的需求凸显了从生物相关来源(如植物来源的天然产物)中识别新型抗病毒药物化合物的重要性。本研究采用生物活性引导的方法,对八种茄科植物的甲醇提取物进行筛选,以鉴定具有抗病毒药物活性的化合物,针对Vero细胞中的DENV-2。五种提取物显著降低了病毒感染性,其中Solanum ovalifolium和Cestrum sp.在非细胞毒性浓度下实现了完全抑制。随后的分级和纯化过程分离出四种螺甾烷型甾体皂苷,其结构通过UPLC-DAD-MS和1D/2D NMR光谱法进行了表征。功能实验表明,这些化合物抑制了DENV的复制,表现为病毒RNA水平的显著降低、NS1和NS3蛋白表达的减少以及传染性病毒滴度的下降。阶段特异性分析显示,其抗病毒药物活性主要与病毒生命周期的细胞内阶段相关,这与抑制病毒复制和/或蛋白加工一致。分子对接分析支持了这些发现,预测了这些化合物与关键病毒酶的有利相互作用,特别是NS5 RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶和NS3解旋酶/蛋白酶。重要的是,分离出的化合物对ZIKV和CHIKV也表现出抗病毒药物活性,表明其对多种虫媒病毒具有交叉疗效。综上所述,这些发现将螺甾烷皂苷识别为有前景的抗病毒药物骨架,并支持其进一步开发为广谱抗病毒药物药物。

papers.title: Circulating apoB-containing lipoproteins constituted blood-borne innate immune barrier limits ZIKV dissemination and congenital infection risk
papers.abstract: Following establishment of primary viremia, flaviviruses require prompt penetration through vascular endothelium to achieve systemic dissemination, yet most infections remain asymptomatic or self-limited. Canonical defenses, including complement and phagocyte clearance, cannot fully explain this containment, suggesting an additional blood-borne antiviral barrier. Here, we identify apoB containing lipoproteins as potent restriction factors against Zika virus (ZIKV), a devastating danger of global pregnancy. By displaying surface accessible phosphatidylserine (PS), they competitively occupy host PS receptors and block entry by viruses exploiting apoptotic mimicry, including flaviviruses, Ebola, and chikungunya virus. In vivo, increasing apoB lipoproteins enhances serum antiviral activity and limits systemic ZIKV dissemination. This barrier extends to the maternal fetal interface, where elevated maternal LDL attenuates vertical transmission and fetal abnormalities. Its efficacy is modulated by gestational fluctuations in maternal LDL level and low abundance in fetal circulating LDL. Collectively, apoB containing lipoproteins form a constitutive blood-borne innate immune barrier that restrains apoptotic-mimicry viruses during the intravascular phase, limits viral dissemination and reduces congenital infection risk. This study provides a rationale for developing diet augmentation strategy to strengthen this innate barrier in at-risk individuals.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which circulating apoB-containing lipoproteins restrict Zika virus (ZIKV) dissemination and congenital infection risk, addressing the gap in understanding the innate immune barriers that limit flavivirus spread during pregnancy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in vitro and in vivo, focusing on the interaction between apoB-containing lipoproteins and viruses such as ZIKV, Ebola, and chikungunya virus. It examined the effects of these lipoproteins on viral entry and dissemination in the context of maternal-fetal transmission.
analysis.methods: The researchers used in vitro assays to assess the interaction between apoB-containing lipoproteins and viral entry, and in vivo models to evaluate the impact of elevated maternal LDL levels on ZIKV dissemination and congenital infection risk.
analysis.main_results: In vivo experiments showed that increasing apoB lipoproteins enhances serum antiviral activity and limits systemic ZIKV dissemination. Additionally, elevated maternal LDL levels were found to reduce vertical transmission and fetal abnormalities.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that apoB-containing lipoproteins act as a blood-borne innate immune barrier against ZIKV, offering a novel mechanism for viral restriction during pregnancy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide a basis for developing dietary strategies to enhance the innate immune barrier against ZIKV in at-risk populations, potentially reducing congenital infection risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's in vivo findings are limited by the use of animal models, and the evidence is moderate due to the lack of direct human clinical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the role of apoB-containing lipoproteins in restricting Zika virus (ZIKV) dissemination and congenital infection risk. It identifies these lipoproteins as a blood-borne innate immune barrier that competes with viral entry by occupying host PS receptors. The research demonstrates that increasing apoB lipoproteins enhances antiviral activity and limits systemic ZIKV spread, with in vivo evidence showing reduced vertical transmission and fetal abnormalities when maternal LDL levels are elevated. The findings suggest a novel mechanism for viral restriction during pregnancy, offering potential for dietary interventions to strengthen this barrier. However, the study's reliance on animal models limits the direct applicability of results to humans, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,含apoB的脂蛋白在ZIKV传播中起到血液固有免疫屏障的作用,为妊娠期间病毒限制提供了新的机制。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为开发饮食策略以增强高风险人群中针对ZIKV的固有免疫屏障提供了依据,可能降低先天感染风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于使用了动物模型,本研究的体内发现存在局限性,且证据强度中等,因为缺乏直接的人类临床数据。

papers.abstract_zh: 在建立原发病毒血症后,黄病毒需要迅速穿透血管内皮以实现全身传播,但大多数感染仍为无症状或自限性。经典的防御机制,包括补体和吞噬细胞清除,无法完全解释这种限制,提示存在额外的血液固有免疫屏障。在此研究中,我们发现含apoB的脂蛋白是限制寨卡病毒(ZIKV)传播的有效因素,ZIKV是全球妊娠的严重威胁。通过在表面展示可接触的磷脂酰丝氨酸(PS),它们竞争性地占据PS受体,阻止利用凋亡模拟机制传播的病毒(包括黄病毒、埃博拉病毒和基孔肯雅病毒)进入。在体内,增加apoB脂蛋白可增强血清抗病毒药物活性并限制ZIKV的全身传播。该屏障也延伸至母胎界面,其中母体LDL水平升高可减轻垂直传播并减少胎儿异常。其效果受到孕期母体LDL水平波动的影响,以及胎儿循环LDL水平较低的限制。总体而言,含apoB的脂蛋白构成了一个固有的血液免疫屏障,限制了在血管内阶段利用凋亡模拟机制的病毒,从而限制病毒传播并降低先天感染风险。本研究为开发饮食增强策略以加强高风险人群的固有免疫屏障提供了依据。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在体外和体内进行,重点研究含apoB脂蛋白与ZIKV、埃博拉病毒和基孔肯雅病毒等病毒的相互作用。它考察了这些脂蛋白在母胎界面背景下对病毒进入和传播的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员使用体外实验评估含apoB脂蛋白与病毒进入的相互作用,并使用体内模型评估母体LDL水平升高对ZIKV传播和先天感染风险的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: 体内实验表明,增加apoB脂蛋白可增强血清抗病毒药物活性并限制ZIKV的全身传播。此外,发现母体LDL水平升高可减少垂直传播并降低胎儿异常的发生率。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,含apoB的脂蛋白在ZIKV传播中起到血液固有免疫屏障的作用,为妊娠期间病毒限制提供了新的机制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为开发饮食策略以增强高风险人群中针对ZIKV的固有免疫屏障提供了依据,可能降低先天感染风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于使用了动物模型,本研究的体内发现存在局限性,且证据强度中等,因为缺乏直接的人类临床数据。

papers.title: Emerging evidence of sand fly fever virus transmission in Sri Lanka
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Sand fly fever virus (SFFV) infection is an acute self-limiting febrile illness caused by phleboviruses and transmitted by sand flies of the Phlebotomus species. The disease has been reported in the Mediterranean region, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, and is now considered to be expanding into new geographic areas. Clinically, SFFV infection closely resembles acute dengue fever. AIM To detect other possible infection including SSFV in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever with negative serology results for NS1 antigen. METHODS In this study, a total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients clinically suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three major hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Patients were from the Colombo and Kandy District, and demographic information was obtained from laboratory request forms, although detailed individual-level demographic data were limited due to anonymization in this laboratory-based study. All samples were initially screened for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further tested for a panel of pathogens including SFFV immunoglobulin (Ig) M, hantavirus IgM, chikungunya IgM, and leptospira IgM antibodies, as well as molecular detection of hantavirus, flavivirus, and alphavirus RNA. RESULTS From tested samples, two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. These two SFFV-positive cases were from Kandy District and included one child (6-8 years) and one adult (40-50 years), both presenting with uncomplicated dengue-like illness. CONCLUSION This study provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka. Given the high endemicity of dengue in the country, SFFV infections may be clinically misdiagnosed as dengue and therefore remain under-recognized. Further studies involving febrile patients and sand fly vector surveillance are required to determine the true burden and epidemiological significance of SFFV in Sri Lanka.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the potential misdiagnosis of SFFV infections as dengue fever, given the clinical similarity between the two and the expanding geographic range of SFFV.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This laboratory-based study collected 757 serum samples from patients suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. The samples were from the Colombo and Kandy Districts, with limited detailed demographic data due to anonymization.
analysis.methods: Samples were first tested for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and then subjected to a panel of serological and molecular assays to detect SFFV-specific IgM antibodies and RNA from other pathogens.
analysis.main_results: Two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as the first documented evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka, highlighting the potential for misdiagnosis with dengue due to clinical similarity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for improved diagnostic protocols to differentiate SFFV from dengue, which could inform better surveillance and management strategies in Sri Lanka.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on anonymized data and the lack of detailed demographic information, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the potential misdiagnosis of SFFV infections as dengue fever in Sri Lanka, given their clinical similarity. A total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients suspected of dengue and admitted to three hospitals in the Colombo and Kandy Districts between January and August 2023. The samples were tested for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further analyzed for SFFV-specific IgM antibodies and other pathogens. Two samples were found to be serologically positive for SFFV, while all other tests were negative. This provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka, suggesting the need for improved diagnostic methods to distinguish it from dengue. The study's findings are limited by the anonymization of data and lack of detailed demographic information, resulting in moderate confidence in the evidence.

papers.title_zh: 斯里兰卡沙蝇热病毒传播的新兴证据
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Sand fly fever virus (SFFV) infection is an acute self-limiting febrile illness caused by phleboviruses and transmitted by sand flies of the Phlebotomus species. The disease has been reported in the Mediterranean region, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Indian subcontinent, and is now considered to be expanding into new geographic areas. Clinically, SFFV infection closely resembles acute dengue fever. AIM To detect other possible infection including SSFV in patients with clinically suspected dengue fever with negative serology results for NS1 antigen. METHODS In this study, a total of 757 serum samples were collected from patients clinically suspected of dengue fever and admitted to three major hospitals in Sri Lanka between January and August 2023. Patients were from the Colombo and Kandy District, and demographic information was obtained from laboratory request forms, although detailed individual-level demographic data were limited due to anonymization in this laboratory-based study. All samples were initially screened for dengue NS1 antigen negativity and further tested for a panel of pathogens including SFFV immunoglobulin (Ig) M, hantavirus IgM, chikungunya IgM, and leptospira IgM antibodies, as well as molecular detection of hantavirus, flavivirus, and alphavirus RNA. RESULTS From tested samples, two samples were serologically positive for SFFV-specific IgM using a commercial immunoblot assay, while all other tests for dengue, chikungunya, leptospira, hantavirus, and related RNA viruses were negative. These two SFFV-positive cases were from Kandy District and included one child (6-8 years) and one adult (40-50 years), both presenting with uncomplicated dengue-like illness. CONCLUSION This study provides the first evidence of SFFV infection in Sri Lanka. Given the high endemicity of dengue in the country, SFFV infections may be clinically misdiagnosed as dengue and therefore remain under-recognized. Further studies involving febrile patients and sand fly vector surveillance are required to determine the true burden and epidemiological significance of SFFV in Sri Lanka.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景 沙蝇热病毒(SFFV)感染是由沙蝇属(Phlebotomus)传播的一种急性自限性发热性疾病,由phleboviruses引起。该疾病已在地中海地区、北非、中东和南亚次大陆被报道,现在被认为正在扩展到新的地理区域。临床表现上,SFFV感染与急性登革热非常相似。目的 检测在临床疑似登革热但NS1抗原检测为阴性的患者中是否存在其他可能的感染,包括SFFV。方法 本研究从2023年1月至8月期间,收集了757份来自斯里兰卡科伦坡和坎迪区三家主要医院的疑似登革热患者血清样本。由于本实验室研究中采用了匿名化处理,因此虽然从实验室申请表中获得了人口统计信息,但详细个体层面的人口统计数据有限。所有样本首先检测登革热NS1抗原阴性,然后进一步检测包括SFFV特异性IgM抗体、汉坦病毒IgM抗体、基孔肯雅病毒IgM抗体和钩端螺旋体IgM抗体在内的多种病原体,以及汉坦病毒、黄病毒和甲病毒的RNA分子检测。结果 在检测的样本中,有2份样本通过商业免疫印迹检测显示SFFV特异性IgM抗体阳性,而所有其他检测登革热、基孔肯雅热、钩端螺旋体、汉坦病毒及相关RNA病毒的结果均为阴性。这2例SFFV阳性病例来自坎迪区,包括一名6-8岁儿童和一名40-50岁成人,均表现为无并发症的登革热样疾病。结论 本研究首次提供了斯里兰卡SFFV感染的证据。鉴于该国登革热的高流行性,SFFV感染可能被误诊为登革热,从而未被充分认识。需要进一步研究发热患者和沙蝇媒介 监测,以确定SFFV在斯里兰卡的真实负担和流行病学意义。

papers.title: Editorial: Exploring the dynamics of emerging and re-emerging diseases: from origins to impact, volume II
papers.abstract: (2026) conducted a review entitled "One Health innovations in tropical disease surveillance for a resilient future". The study explores current tropical disease surveillance approaches that adopt a "One Health" perspective. They concluded that an effective 'One Health' strategy should be proactive rather than reactive, incorporating climate intelligence and addressing the behavioral and social drivers of disease, while also being supported by multilateral cooperation and policy continuity. The authors emphasized the importance of cross-sectoral integration to improve the early detection and response to disease. Furthermore, they argue that technologies, including artificial intelligence, genomic sequencing, environmental biosensors, and mobile health platforms, are enhancing the speed and scalability of disease detection, response, and the prevention of cross-species transmission. The study also highlighted the critical need for interdisciplinary education, policy support, and real-time data sharing to build system-wide resilience. They recommend involving local communities in ecologically sensitive tropical issues and in formulating context-specific surveillance strategies. Lastly, they argue that embedding 'One Health' principles into surveillance practices transforms reactive systems into resilient ones. (2026) conducted a study entitled "Development and validation of a novel multiplex PCR assay for the detection of Anaplasma, Babesia and Theileria in captive wild ungulates". The researchers developed a multiplex PCR (mPCR) assay to detect Babesia, Theileria and Anaplasma pathogens simultaneously at the genus level in wild ungulates. For piroplasmids (Babesia and Theileria), two pairs of primers were designed using the 18S ribosomal RNA gene. These primers were specific and sensitive and could generate target products of 178 bp for Theileria and 479 bp for Babesia. Additionally, a primer pair targeting the 16S rRNA gene was designed to generate an expected 318 bp product for Anaplasma. These three primer pairs were tested using blood samples collected from 60 captive Gazella bennettii (Family Bovidae) and Axis porcinus (Family Cervidae) from various wildlife parks and zoos in Punjab, Pakistan. The mPCR results produced by these primers were consistent with those from monoplex PCR, with an overall hemoparasites prevalence of 66.66% (40/60). Sequencing of the PCR products confirmed these results, providing a valuable complementary tool for the simultaneous, accurate and routine detection of Anaplasma and piroplasms in endangered wild ungulates. 2026) presented a clinical case report entitled "Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease following venison exposure in a chronic wasting disease-endemic region: a zoonotic surveillance perspective". This study involved a thorough evaluation of the clinical progression, diagnostic assessment, and public health investigation of a patient with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), which is a fatal condition caused by prions. The results they published showed that the 72year-old hunter developed progressive rapid dementia and startle myoclonus. During hospitalization, the patient developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Magnetic resonance imaging showed cortical ribboning and diffusion restriction in the basal ganglia, while cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers (RT-QuIC, total tau and 14-3-3) and post-mortem neuropathology confirmed sporadic CJD of the MM1 subtype. The public health implications of the disease were discussed at length, particularly regarding hunters with extensive exposure to cervids. 2026) conducted a study in Qinghai Province, China titled "Mpox-HIV coinfection in a low-incidence setting: epidemiological insights from Qinghai, China". The study examined the epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of mpox-HIV coinfection in a male patient who had sex with men, as well as systemic gaps in surveillance, diagnosis, and the response to the infection. The patient presented with a fever of 39.4°C and the recovery of mpox virus (MPXV) nucleic acid was confirmed following the collection of a nasopharyngeal swab specimen. Further characterization and identification of the virus revealed it to be MPXV clade IIb (formerly known as the West African clade), C.1.1 sub lineage, with the full designation B.1.3.1.1. As the authors suggest, the findings of this study indicate that the most likely route of exposure for the patient was high-risk sexual contact within a social or sexual network, since no history of international travel was recorded. This finding suggests that silent transmission may already be occurring in regions with low incidence. 2026) conducted a study on the rates of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection and its relationship with vaccination status. They retrospectively analyzed data from patients who experienced reinfection during the second and third waves of the pandemic. Of the 458 participants in the study, 62 (13.54%) who had a primary infection were confirmed to have had a reinfection. Furthermore, 60 participants (13%) were asymptomatic, while 398 participants (87%) were symptomatic, with fever being the most frequently observed symptom during both primary (70.3%) and reinfection (72.58%) infections. Lastly, an association was observed between infection status and vomiting symptoms, which was statistically significant (p < 0.01).Carrero and Mosquera's (2026) article was a review of the re-emergence of arboviruses in the Andean-Amazonian corridor in Latin America. Datasets on various vector-borne diseases from selected countries were analyze from 2023 to 2026 to comprehend epidemiological trends of reemerging diseases. The results showed persistence of malaria in Amazonian areas as well as a sustained increase in arboviruses infection such as yellow fever, dengue and chikungunya. For instance, 132 confirmed human cases of yellow fever outbreak was recorded in Colombia from 2024 to 2025 while 65 death was registered in Ecuador from 37,840 cases of dengue. Furthermore, signs of reemergence of yellow fever were observed in Venezuela during 2025 and 2026 which was attributed to the sylvatic cycles of the virus. The study revealed that the re-emergence of some arboviruses is linked to ecological, social and health factors, as well as poor health education, vaccine hesitancy, limited access to health services, the infodemic and weaknesses in epidemiological surveillance and vector control. In conclusion, the Research Topic has explored the complex and multifaceted aspects of emerging and re-emerging of vector-borne diseases. Also, this topic has provided deeper understanding of the ecological, genetic, environmental and socioeconomic factors that drive the emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases while exploring their cascading effects on public health, societies, and economies.

papers.title_zh: 编者按:探索新兴和再新兴疾病的动态:从起源到影响,第二卷
papers.source_body_en: (2026) conducted a review entitled "One Health innovations in tropical disease surveillance for a resilient future". The study explores current tropical disease surveillance approaches that adopt a "One Health" perspective. They concluded that an effective 'One Health' strategy should be proactive rather than reactive, incorporating climate intelligence and addressing the behavioral and social drivers of disease, while also being supported by multilateral cooperation and policy continuity. The authors emphasized the importance of cross-sectoral integration to improve the early detection and response to disease. Furthermore, they argue that technologies, including artificial intelligence, genomic sequencing, environmental biosensors, and mobile health platforms, are enhancing the speed and scalability of disease detection, response, and the prevention of cross-species transmission. The study also highlighted the critical need for interdisciplinary education, policy support, and real-time data sharing to build system-wide resilience. They recommend involving local communities in ecologically sensitive tropical issues and in formulating context-specific surveillance strategies. Lastly, they argue that embedding 'One Health' principles into surveillance practices transforms reactive systems into resilient ones. (2026) conducted a study entitled "Development and validation of a novel multiplex PCR assay for the detection of Anaplasma, Babesia and Theileria in captive wild ungulates". The researchers developed a multiplex PCR (mPCR) assay to detect Babesia, Theileria and Anaplasma pathogens simultaneously at the genus level in wild ungulates. For piroplasmids (Babesia and Theileria), two pairs of primers were designed using the 18S ribosomal RNA gene. These primers were specific and sensitive and could generate target products of 178 bp for Theileria and 479 bp for Babesia. Additionally, a primer pair targeting the 16S rRNA gene was designed to generate an expected 318 bp product for Anaplasma. These three primer pairs were tested using blood samples collected from 60 captive Gazella bennettii (Family Bovidae) and Axis porcinus (Family Cervidae) from various wildlife parks and zoos in Punjab, Pakistan. The mPCR results produced by these primers were consistent with those from monoplex PCR, with an overall hemoparasites prevalence of 66.66% (40/60). Sequencing of the PCR products confirmed these results, providing a valuable complementary tool for the simultaneous, accurate and routine detection of Anaplasma and piroplasms in endangered wild ungulates. 2026) presented a clinical case report entitled "Sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease following venison exposure in a chronic wasting disease-endemic region: a zoonotic surveillance perspective". This study involved a thorough evaluation of the clinical progression, diagnostic assessment, and public health investigation of a patient with Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD), which is a fatal condition caused by prions. The results they published showed that the 72year-old hunter developed progressive rapid dementia and startle myoclonus. During hospitalization, the patient developed posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES). Magnetic resonance imaging showed cortical ribboning and diffusion restriction in the basal ganglia, while cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers (RT-QuIC, total tau and 14-3-3) and post-mortem neuropathology confirmed sporadic CJD of the MM1 subtype. The public health implications of the disease were discussed at length, particularly regarding hunters with extensive exposure to cervids. 2026) conducted a study in Qinghai Province, China titled "Mpox-HIV coinfection in a low-incidence setting: epidemiological insights from Qinghai, China". The study examined the epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of mpox-HIV coinfection in a male patient who had sex with men, as well as systemic gaps in surveillance, diagnosis, and the response to the infection. The patient presented with a fever of 39.4°C and the recovery of mpox virus (MPXV) nucleic acid was confirmed following the collection of a nasopharyngeal swab specimen. Further characterization and identification of the virus revealed it to be MPXV clade IIb (formerly known as the West African clade), C.1.1 sub lineage, with the full designation B.1.3.1.1. As the authors suggest, the findings of this study indicate that the most likely route of exposure for the patient was high-risk sexual contact within a social or sexual network, since no history of international travel was recorded. This finding suggests that silent transmission may already be occurring in regions with low incidence. 2026) conducted a study on the rates of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection and its relationship with vaccination status. They retrospectively analyzed data from patients who experienced reinfection during the second and third waves of the pandemic. Of the 458 participants in the study, 62 (13.54%) who had a primary infection were confirmed to have had a reinfection. Furthermore, 60 participants (13%) were asymptomatic, while 398 participants (87%) were symptomatic, with fever being the most frequently observed symptom during both primary (70.3%) and reinfection (72.58%) infections. Lastly, an association was observed between infection status and vomiting symptoms, which was statistically significant (p < 0.01).Carrero and Mosquera's (2026) article was a review of the re-emergence of arboviruses in the Andean-Amazonian corridor in Latin America. Datasets on various vector-borne diseases from selected countries were analyze from 2023 to 2026 to comprehend epidemiological trends of reemerging diseases. The results showed persistence of malaria in Amazonian areas as well as a sustained increase in arboviruses infection such as yellow fever, dengue and chikungunya. For instance, 132 confirmed human cases of yellow fever outbreak was recorded in Colombia from 2024 to 2025 while 65 death was registered in Ecuador from 37,840 cases of dengue. Furthermore, signs of reemergence of yellow fever were observed in Venezuela during 2025 and 2026 which was attributed to the sylvatic cycles of the virus. The study revealed that the re-emergence of some arboviruses is linked to ecological, social and health factors, as well as poor health education, vaccine hesitancy, limited access to health services, the infodemic and weaknesses in epidemiological surveillance and vector control. In conclusion, the Research Topic has explored the complex and multifaceted aspects of emerging and re-emerging of vector-borne diseases. Also, this topic has provided deeper understanding of the ecological, genetic, environmental and socioeconomic factors that drive the emergence and re-emergence of infectious diseases while exploring their cascading effects on public health, societies, and economies.

papers.title: Standardizing the Approach to Acute Undifferentiated Febrile Illness: Development of an Expert Consensus-Based Algorithm for India.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute Undifferentiated Febrile Illness (AUFI) poses an immense challenge to diagnosis in India because it can be caused by various pathogens. The clinical presentation is often similar across causes, and the number of potential causative organisms continues to increase due to changes in climate and ecology. To counter these challenges, it was necessary that a holistic diagnostic algorithm based on a set of predefined criteria be formulated by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR). METHODS: A Core Committee and Expert Committee were formed with members including infectious disease specialists, clinical microbiologists, radiologists, and public health experts who reviewed national and international guidelines, statistics on instances and prevalence, and recommendations from ICMR. A structured sequence of consultations during 2022 and 2024 led to formulation of an expert consensus-based algorithm as per pathogens prioritization. The algorithm considers various factors pertaining to disease diagnosis and treatment. RESULTS AND DISCUSSIONS: The list of priority pathogens includes dengue, chikungunya, influenza, enteric fever, scrub typhus, leptospirosis, malaria, brucellosis, and some unusual causes like CCHF, KFD, melioidosis, and rickettsial infections. The algorithm recommends a structured method for taking a history, lists warning signs requiring hospital admission, and recommends case-specific diagnostic and treatment guidelines for stable and severe patients. Its main objective is to address diagnostic delay, empiric use of antimicrobials, and risk of complications like sepsis and multi-organ dysfunction. CONCLUSION: The AUFI diagnostic algorithm is a systematic and specific tool that aims at optimizing early pathogen identification and promoting correct decisions with regards to appropriate clinical practice directly affecting patient care. It will also be useful for optimizing surveillance, thereby affecting public health and optimizing patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:急性未分化发热疾病(AUFI)在印度对诊断构成巨大挑战,因为它可能由多种病原体引起。临床表现常在不同病因之间相似,且由于气候和生态变化,潜在致病微生物的数量持续增加。为应对这些挑战,印度医学研究理事会(ICMR)有必要制定一套基于预定义标准的整体诊断算法。方法:成立了核心委员会和专家委员会,成员包括传染病专家、临床微生物学家、放射科医生和公共卫生专家,审查了国内外指南、病例统计和患病率以及ICMR的建议。2022年至2024年的一系列结构化协商导致形成了基于专家共识的、按病原体优先级排序的算法。该算法考虑了与疾病诊断和治疗相关的多种因素。结果与讨论:优先病原体名单包括登革热、基孔肯雅热、流感、肠热伤寒、斑疹伤寒、钩端螺旋体病、疟疾、布鲁氏菌病以及一些不常见的原因,如CCHF、KFD、梅毒样杆菌病和立克次体感染。该算法推荐了系统的病史采集方法,列出了需要住院的警示体征,并为稳定患者和重症患者提供了针对性诊断和治疗指南。其主要目标是解决诊断延误、经验性使用抗菌药物以及败血症和多器官功能障碍等并发症的风险。结论:AUFI诊断算法是一种系统且专用的工具,旨在优化早期病原体识别,促进在适当临床实践中的正确决策,直接影响患者护理。它还将有助于优化监测,从而影响公共卫生并优化患者结局。

papers.full_text: 1 © 2026 Indian Journal of Medical Research, published by Scientific Scholar for Director-General, Indian Council of Medical Research This open access publication is protected under CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 Editorial ICMR Institutes: From research to impact- National Institute of Virology, Pune Shweta Tanwar1 1Indian Journal of Medical Research, Indian Council of Medical Research, New Delhi, India Received August 28, 2026; Accepted August 28, 2026; Ahead of print September 18, 2026; Published *** *, 2026 Indian J Med Res 164, ****, 2026, pp **-** DOI: 10.25259/IJMR_3319_2026 How to cite this article: Tanwar S. ICMR Institutes: From research to impact- National Institute of Virology, Pune. Indian J Med Res. doi: 10.25259/ IJMR_3319_2026 Emerging and re-emerging viral infections have repeatedly tested India's capacity for rapid diagnosis, surveillance and outbreak response. Over the past decade, the COVID-19 pandemic and outbreaks of Nipah virus disease, Zika virus infection, Chandipura virus and other vector-borne and zoonotic infections have shown that preparedness depends not only on scientific discovery, but on the ability to translate laboratory evidence into deployable diagnostics, surveillance systems and timely public-health action. Established in 1952 as the Virus Research Centre and renamed the National Institute of Virology (NIV) in 1978, ICMR–NIV, Pune, has evolved into India's premier virology institute, integrating basic research with the development of medical countermeasures, outbreak investigation and pandemic preparedness. Over the past decade, its research and scientific capabilities have contributed across this continuum from diagnostic preparedness and genomic surveillance to field-based outbreak response and the detection of emerging viral threats. It serves as the national resource centre for a network of 167 Virus Research and Diagnostic Laboratories (VRDLs) and 23 biosafety level-3 laboratories, and maintains a national repository of authenticated virus strains supporting the indigenous development of diagnostics, vaccines and therapeutics (Box). This article examines key examples from the past decade illustrating how sustained virological research and institutional capacity have supported public-health action during outbreaks while strengthening national preparedness. Building pandemic preparedness: from diagnostic science to a national response: The early COVID-19 pandemic tested whether pre-existing scientific capacity could be rapidly converted into a population- level response. India required validated diagnostic protocols, quality-assured testing and mechanisms for expanding laboratory capacity across a geographically diverse country. NIV supported standardisation of molecular testing across the VRDL network; indigenous in vitro-transcribed RNA controls provided a positive-control resource when access to such material was constrained.1,2 National laboratory surveillance expanded from around 250 tests per day in early March 2020 to 50,000 per day by end-April, with 99% of districts reporting testing by then,3 a national, multi- institutional achievement to which NIV's reference- laboratory functions contributed. NIV also drove the shift from diagnosis to molecular epidemiology and countermeasure development. Sequencing and isolation of the first SARS-CoV-2 viruses from India supported further research on diagnostics, antivirals and vaccines,4,5 while genomic surveillance characterised the B.1.617 lineage and key spike mutations during Maharashtra's second wave.6 The Institute also contributed to the development of indigenous vaccines, including the inactivated vaccine Covaxin,7,8 and the world's first approved DNA vaccine against SARS-CoV-2, and has continuously tracked emerging variants and vaccine-induced immune responses to inform booster-dose policy. A complementary translational effort saw NIV develop an indigenous IgG-based antibody assay for past SARS- CoV-2 infection, transfer the technology to industry and validate it for field use — enabling the serosurveillance studies that helped inform containment and mitigation strategy across the country.9-11 Together, these contributions illustrate a continuum from standardised 2 INDIAN J MED RES, MONTH 2026 testing and diagnostic scale-up to genomic intelligence and indigenous countermeasure development and how laboratory research can become embedded in systems for epidemic response and public-health decision-making. Responding to high-consequence zoonoses: The Nipah experience: If COVID-19 demonstrated the importance of scale, Nipah virus disease has repeatedly demonstrated the importance of speed. Across outbreaks in Kerala and West Bengal since 2018, NIV teams have combined rapid laboratory confirmation with serosurveillance of contacts and surveillance of Pteropus bat populations, extending the response beyond human case confirmation to the animal–human interface.12,13 A field laboratory established during the earliest outbreaks gave way, from 2023 onward, to a rapidly deployable mobile BSL-3 laboratory that enabled onsite diagnosis within approximately four hours during the Kozhikode outbreak.14 This capability in high-containment science and field deployment also positions NIV to strengthen national multisectoral preparedness through structured One Health mock drills such as ‘Vishanu Yuddh Abhyas’- the 2024 edition of which demonstrated the value of coordinating human-health, animal-husbandry and wildlife sectors around a simulated zoonotic outbreak with regular NIV participation in such exercises identified as a priority for strengthening interagency coordination. The significance lies not simply in faster diagnosis, but in shortening the interval between suspicion and actionable evidence and how reference- laboratory expertise can evolve into a more distributed, multisectoral preparedness model. Adapting surveillance to emerging and re-emerging threats: NIV's surveillance has repeatedly adapted to shifting viral and vector ecologies. Expanded Zika screening identified infections in newer geographical settings, as well as dengue–chikungunya co- infections. The 2024 Pune outbreak reflected this, integrating molecular, epidemiological and genomic characterisation.15,16 A decade of chikungunya serosurveillance in Pune documented rising population exposure, while genomic studies tracked viral resurgence and evolution.17,18 For Kyasanur Forest disease (KFD), phylogeographic analysis traced spread beyond its historical focus into Sindhudurg district of Maharashtra, prompting state action on vaccinating high-risk forest and health workers.19,20 A multicentre field evaluation showed high performance for a portable point-of-care assay.21 An adjuvant whole-virion vaccine candidate developed with Indian Immunologicals Ltd has now completed preclinical safety and efficacy evaluation.22 Sustained VRDL-based surveillance for respiratory illness also functioned as a sentinel for zoonotic spillover. In 2024, a routine sample led to confirmation of India's second human case of avian influenza A(H9N2), with genomic characterisation and antiviral- susceptibility testing informing risk assessment.23 NIV has similarly identified and characterised outbreaks of Chandipura virus, including India's largest, in Gujarat in 2024,24 and the aetiological agents behind India's largest Guillain-Barré syndrome outbreak, contributing directly to outbreak containment.25 Diagnostic development also kept pace with newly emerging global threats: indigenous IgM/IgG ELISAs for mpox virus extended national testing capacity for this newly emerging orthopoxvirus.26 Together, these examples show how NIV's surveillance has evolved from confirming known threats to detecting the unexpected, serology tracking population exposure, genomics tracing viral spread, and routine networks doubling as sentinels for emerging pathogens. Beyond outbreak response: national systems and self- reliance: Much of NIV's public-health value lies in infrastructure sustained between emergencies. Over the past decade, it has trained more than 6,000 personnel from VRDL laboratories nationwide and produced and supplied nearly 1.24 lakh MAC-ELISA kits for dengue, chikungunya and Japanese encephalitis to national surveillance programmes. Its Mumbai Unit is one of only seven WHO Global Specialised Laboratories for polio worldwide and the only one in a developing country. The Unit sustains Acute Flaccid Paralysis and environmental surveillance, and established India's iVDPV surveillance network, a global first. It also serves as the WHO Regional Reference Laboratory for measles and rubella for South-East Asia, having supported expansion of the regional network from 12 to 28 accredited laboratories. Beyond surveillance, the Institute's virus repository supplied 27 authenticated strains to 18 institutions in 2025–26 alone, while a growing portfolio of technologies and patents spanning multiplex diagnostic assays, novel antivirals and vaccine candidates continues to move toward industry transfer and licensing. Together, these functions have strengthened India's self-reliance in biomedical research well beyond any single outbreak response. From episodic response to durable preparedness: Different threats have demanded different capabilities: COVID-19 required scale and decentralisation; 3 TANWAR: FROM RESEARCH TO IMPACT Nipah required speed and proximity; arboviral and zoonotic threats required surveillance responsive to shifting epidemiology; and sustained networks proved essential for recognising the unexpected. National responses inevitably depend on the combined efforts of governments, laboratories, clinicians and communities. Even so, NIV's trajectory over the past decade illustrates how sustained investment in reference diagnostics, laboratory networks, genomics, high-containment science and field investigation generates value that extends well beyond individual publications — strengthening the systems through which India detects, interprets and responds to emerging viral threats. Looking ahead — director's perspective: ‘Over the next five years, ICMR–NIV will prioritise the development of indigenous medical countermeasures, including antiviral therapeutics, next-generation vaccine platforms, monoclonal antibodies, and rapid, affordable diagnostics, while advancing fundamental virology to deepen understanding of virus–host interactions, viral evolution, pathogenesis, and protective immune responses. Emerging opportunities in genomics, artificial intelligence, advanced disease modelling, and integrated One Health surveillance will support the early detection and effective control of emerging infections. The Institute will further strengthen biorepositories, high-containment laboratory capacity, and scientific training through strategic partnerships with academia, industry, and public-health agencies. By providing scientific leadership and coordinating the Zonal NIV network, ICMR–NIV will accelerate innovation and strengthen India’s preparedness and response to future outbreaks and pandemics.’ (Dr Naveen Kumar, Director, ICMR–National Institute of Virology, Pune) Financial support and sponsorship: None.
